teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The whole 2-year, 120-ECTS second-cycle degree is delivered in English: the official programme page states 'Fully taught in English, the program prepares graduates who are professionally competent in English...' and the Apply@UniTo course record lists 'Study language: English'. It is a single University of Turin degree run by the Department of Foreign Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures (Dipartimento di Lingue e Letterature straniere e Culture moderne) - NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and NOT an interuniversity/joint programme. Note that the degree sits in the same Italian degree class (LM-37) as the Italian-language 'Lingue e letterature moderne' programme, but it is a separate, distinctly coded degree course (code 1007M22) with its own admission procedure, its own admission interview calendar and its own e-mail contact (ammissioni.eas@unito.it). No knowledge of Italian is required for admission: UNITO explicitly states that for applicants with a foreign qualification the admission interview normally also tests Italian at C1, but 'la conoscenza della lingua italiana non e necessaria per il percorso LM-37 English and American Studies (fully taught in English)'. One caveat: the Italian-language CampusNet metadata block on the programme page still lists 'Lingua: italiano' - this is a catalogue/database artefact contradicted by the programme's own English description, by the Apply@UniTo record and by the department's admission rules. Once enrolled, international students must take 'Italian for International Students' (3 credits) as a compulsory curricular activity, but this is a study-plan obligation, not an entry requirement.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. Official teaching seat (sede didattica): Torino - Complesso Aldo Moro, via Sant'Ottavio corner of via Verdi. Teaching and language laboratories also take place at Palazzo Nuovo / Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA-UniTO), via Sant'Ottavio 20, and admission language-level tests are held in Aula Informatica 1 (1st floor), Complesso Aldo Moro, via Sant'Ottavio 18, or in the CLA rooms at Palazzo Nuovo. Responsible department: Dipartimento di Lingue e Letterature straniere e Culture moderne, University of Turin.
degree_class: LM-37 (Lingue e letterature moderne europee e americane / Modern European and American Languages and Literatures). UNITO internal programme code: 1007M22. Type of degree: Laurea magistrale (second-cycle / postgraduate degree), 2 years, 120 ECTS, teaching mode 'convenzionale' (conventional, in presence). Academic year shown on the official programme record at the time of research: 2025/2026.
admission_type: Open access with verification of minimum requirements ('accesso libero con verifica di requisiti minimi'). There is no numerus clausus and no ranked competition, but admission is NOT automatic: candidates must (a) satisfy quantified curricular credit thresholds, (b) for international applicants hold a valid C1 English certificate, and (c) pass an admission interview before an admissions committee. No TOLC and no SAT are used at master's level (TOLC-SU applies only to the department's bachelor's programmes). Two entirely separate application channels exist and applicants must use the correct one: (1) applicants holding a BA issued by an ITALIAN university apply through the UNITO portal (www.unito.it / MyUniTo) with a 'Domanda di ammissione preliminare', then take a CLA language-level test and an admission interview booked via a Google Form; (2) applicants holding a BA issued by a NON-ITALIAN institution, and all international students, must apply through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course id 671). The department warns: 'If you are an international applicant, DO NOT USE the application procedure described on this page: your application will be disregarded.' A territory quota applies on the international channel: a maximum of 30 non-European applicants residing abroad will be admitted.
application_deadline_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027 there are two distinct EU-relevant deadlines depending on where the bachelor's degree was issued. (A) FOREIGN QUALIFICATION, applying via Apply@UniTo - the currently open window is the Fourth admission call, reserved to open access postgraduate degree programmes: 25 August - 8 September 2026, and the EAS course page shows the hard deadline as 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time, with the notice that this call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. The same group could alternatively have used the First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, which was open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes. A non-refundable EUR 60 application fee must be paid within the deadline of the call. (B) ITALIAN QUALIFICATION, applying via MyUniTo - the 'Domanda di ammissione preliminare' opens in early June and closes on 31 December of the application year, with actual enrolment (immatricolazione) running from 23 July 2026, 9:30 to 14 January 2027, 15:00 and the first instalment due by 14 January 2027; interviews are held on a small number of published dates spread from July to November plus a January slot. The exact 2026/2027 EAS interview dates and the exact opening date of the 2026/2027 preliminary application were NOT recoverable: the most recent accessible version of the department's admission page (last updated 4 May 2026) still displayed the 2025/2026 calendar - preliminary application from 2 July 2025 to 31 December 2025, EAS interviews on 14 July 2025 at 11:00, 17 September 2025 at 12:00, 9 October 2025 at 17:45 and 27 November 2025 at 17:45, with January 2026 slots arranged by writing to ammissioni.eas@unito.it, and enrolment confirmable from 25 July 2025, 9:30 to 16 January 2026, 15:00. Applicants with an Italian degree must check the live page for the 2026/2027 dates. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027, non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants) could only use the First admission call on Apply@UniTo: 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026. That was the only 2026/2027 window described as 'open to all applicants wishing to apply for postgraduate degree programs'; the third, fourth and fifth calls are all explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy', and the EAS course page carries the warning 'If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' Successful non-EU applicants must in addition complete the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform within the ministerial deadline and complete visa formalities at the competent Italian diplomatic mission. As of the research date (1 September 2026) the non-EU-abroad window for 2026/2027 is closed; the equivalent 2027/2028 first call would be expected around late November 2027 - late January 2028 but is not yet published. This deadline is derived from the university-wide Apply@UniTo call calendar rather than from an EAS-specific statement. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised entrance examination: no TOLC, no GRE, no GMAT, no SAT, and no written admission test at master's level. The selection instruments are an ADMISSION INTERVIEW plus, for applicants with an Italian degree only, a computer-based LANGUAGE LEVEL TEST. (1) ADMISSION INTERVIEW - compulsory for all candidates. 'An admissions committee will evaluate applications, based on curriculum and an interview.' The department describes the interview as having a knowledge/orientation function, focused on the overall assessment of the candidate's profile on the basis of previous academic career and motivation for choosing the master's programme, and states that enrolment is subordinate to passing an interview verifying the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation. For EAS, applicants with an Italian degree book their interview themselves via an online Google Form at least 48 hours before the published dates (all other LM programmes of the department are convoked directly by the programme president). Interviews for the Italian channel are held IN PERSON, and candidates receive a confirmation e-mail the day before with time and venue. Dates and times cannot be changed. (2) CLA LANGUAGE LEVEL TEST - a 40-minute, 30-question multiple-choice computer test on vocabulary, grammar and comprehension, developed with the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, taken in person, once only per language, with results banded 81-100% / 61-80% / 40-60% / <40% (below 40% signals difficulty in continuing to master's level). The result is an element of evaluation available to the committee, not a pass/fail gate. Expected level for English is C1. IMPORTANT EXEMPTION: 'non svolgono il test le studentesse e gli studenti con titolo estero' - candidates holding a foreign qualification do NOT sit the CLA test; instead they must submit an accepted international C1 certificate through Apply@UniTo. Candidates transferring from another master's programme or another university are also exempt. Test venues and support: testmagistrali.lingue@unito.it. (3) The interview format for the international (Apply@UniTo) channel is not separately specified on the EAS pages; the international selection is described as committee evaluation of the application file plus an interview. Contact for EAS admission matters: ammissioni.eas@unito.it.
academic_requirements:
1) QUALIFICATION - candidates must have completed, PRIOR TO ADMISSION, at least a three-year university degree ('laurea o diploma universitario'), i.e. a first-cycle/bachelor's degree earned after at least 3 years of university education. If issued abroad, the degree must come from an academically recognised institution under the rules in force for admission to Italian universities. Candidates who have not yet graduated may submit the preliminary application and sit the interview, but can only complete enrolment after obtaining the first-level qualification and in any case no later than the enrolment deadline set by the Academic Senate.

2) CURRICULAR CREDIT REQUIREMENTS - two different formulations apply depending on where the degree was earned.
   (a) Degree obtained IN THE EUROPEAN UNION (including Italy): at least 18 credits in English language/linguistics AND at least 18 credits in British, English postcolonial or North American literatures. On the department's Italian-language 'requisiti minimi' page the same rule is expressed by SSD code: at least 18 CFU of Lingua Inglese (L-LIN/12) and at least 18 CFU of Letteratura inglese (L-LIN/10) and/or Letteratura anglo-americana (L-LIN/11). Holders of an Italian L-11 bachelor's degree in Lingue e Letterature Moderne with full recognition of credits satisfy the requirement automatically.
   (b) Degree obtained OUTSIDE THE EUROPEAN UNION: the equivalent of at least 10% of the total degree credit/hour load in English language/linguistics AND the equivalent of at least 10% of the total degree credit/hour load in British, English postcolonial or North American literatures.
   (c) The Apply@UniTo international channel merges the two into a single 'you must meet ALL of the following' rule: the equivalent of at least 18 ECTS credits (or 10 percent of total degree credits/hours) in English and/or American language/linguistics; the equivalent of at least 18 ECTS credits (or 10 percent of total degree credits/hours) in British, English postcolonial or North American literatures; plus an international English-language certification.

3) MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FORM - international applicants must complete and upload a dedicated 'Application for LM-37 English and American Studies post-graduate degree' form issued by the department. It must be filled out IN FULL and the application will not be processed without it. It asks for: how the applicant's GPA ranks in their own university's grading system (Excellent - top 5% / Very good - top 20% / Good - top 40% / Other); the total number of credits or hours in the bachelor's degree; an itemised list of up to five courses (with credits/hours) satisfying Requirement 1 (10% of total credit load in English language and linguistics - the form's own worked example: 'if your degree transcript lists a total of 130 credits, at least 13 must meet this requirement'); an itemised list of up to five courses satisfying Requirement 2 (10% of total credit load in English or North American literature); and a yes/no declaration of holding a qualifying English certificate. The form warns: 'if this form does not provide sufficient evidence that you meet the minimum credit and language requirements, you will not be eligible for admission to the program.'

4) GPA / GRADE THRESHOLD - no published numerical GPA cut-off. Grade standing is captured indirectly through the GPA-ranking band on the minimum requirements form and through the committee's overall assessment of the candidate's profile at interview.

5) PLACES AND QUOTAS - the programme is open access with no overall restricted number of places. A territory quota applies on the international channel: 'This program will admit a maximum of 30 non-European residing abroad applicants.' No separate Marco Polo quota is published for this programme.

6) MAKING UP MISSING CREDITS - Italian-channel candidates who lack the required CFU may take 'esami singoli' (single exams) at UNITO or another university to fill the gap; the preliminary application and the interview may be taken before those exams are sat, and enrolment follows once the credits are obtained and reported to the student office. Requests go through the MyUniTo help desk (UNITO students) or servizistudenti.scienzeumanistiche@unito.it (students from other universities).

7) RECOGNITION OF FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS - after submission, UNITO may require further documents such as a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Verification / Statement of Comparability, and the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment step.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - the requirement differs sharply by channel, and this is the single most important distinction for this programme.
  (a) INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS (foreign qualification, Apply@UniTo): a valid international certification attesting AT LEAST CEFR C1 is MANDATORY, and the certificate must be NO MORE THAN THREE YEARS OLD. UNITO states 'NO OTHER CERTIFICATIONS are accepted' beyond the following closed list: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); PTE Academic with a minimum score of 76; IELTS with a minimum score of 7 out of 9 and no component lower than 6; TOEFL iBT with a minimum score of 95 out of 120 and no component lower than 17; Trinity College, at least ISE III / GESE grade 10 or 11. The departmental minimum requirements form restates the point bluntly: 'Applicants who do not submit a valid language certification will not be admitted.' Note that this C1 bar with a closed certificate list is considerably stricter than the B2 level typical of other English-taught UNITO master's programmes.
  (b) APPLICANTS WITH A DEGREE OBTAINED IN THE EUROPEAN UNION (including Italy): the official programme page states explicitly '(no language certification is required)' for this group. Their English is instead assessed through the compulsory CLA language level test (expected level for English: C1) and the admission interview, which includes a test of the level of knowledge of the foreign language(s) to be studied.
  No exemption is published for native speakers or for graduates of English-medium bachelor's programmes on the international channel - the certificate list is presented as closed.

ITALIAN - no Italian language requirement for admission. UNITO's general rule for the department's master's programmes is that candidates with a foreign qualification must also demonstrate Italian at C1 in the interview, but the rule carries an explicit carve-out: 'la conoscenza della lingua italiana non e necessaria per il percorso LM-37 English and American Studies (fully taught in English)'. Italian is instead a curricular obligation after enrolment: 'Italian For International Students (3 credits) is mandatory for all international students', with beginner and pre-intermediate levels offered in the first-year study plan.
required_documents:
A) INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS / FOREIGN QUALIFICATION (Apply@UniTo, apply.unito.it course 671). UNITO requires the attachments to be uploaded IN THE FOLLOWING ORDER: (1) the completed departmental MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FORM - 'Form must be filled out in full, and application will not be processed without this attachment'; (2) the international English language certification (C1, from the closed accepted list, issued within the last three years); (3) transcript of records in English (or Italian); (4) copy of passport; (5) all other relevant documents. In addition, under the university-wide rules for postgraduate applications: a MOTIVATION LETTER, which for this programme must be in English ('A motivation letter must be added to your application. The motivation letter must be in English.'); the first-cycle degree certificate / diploma obtained after at least 3 years of university study; the documents required for the applicant's specific foreign education system; optionally the degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution with a translation. Entry qualification documents are accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; a document in any other language must be uploaded both in the original and in certified translation. A non-refundable EUR 60 application fee must be paid within the call deadline. After submission UNITO may request a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Verification / Statement of Comparability, and the International Students Office may request more documents at the enrolment step. Incomplete applications are not processed.

B) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN QUALIFICATION (MyUniTo / www.unito.it): (1) the 'Domanda di ammissione preliminare' (preliminary admission application), in which the candidate enters the full list of exams passed, specifying the SSD (scientific-disciplinary sector) and CFU of each; (2) the 'Dichiarazione delle lingue di studio per Corsi di Laurea magistrale' (declaration of study languages), which must be attached to the preliminary application; (3) proof of having sat the CLA language level test (booked through the form on the CLA-UniTO page); (4) the interview booking made via the EAS online Google Form at least 48 hours before the chosen date, submitted AFTER the preliminary application; (5) where credits are still missing, evidence of single exams passed, notified to the student office before enrolment. No English certificate is required from this group.

uncertainty_notes:
SOURCE ACCESS SITUATION
- apply.unito.it was reachable directly via curl with a standard desktop browser User-Agent (HTTP 200). The Apply@UniTo course page for English and American Studies (course id 671), the 2026/2027 call calendar and the required-documentation page were read first-hand and in full on 1 September 2026. WebFetch alone returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) for the same URLs, so the User-Agent workaround was essential.
- www.lingue.unito.it (the official programme host, i.e. official_program_url) was completely unreachable at network level (connection failure, curl exit 0 bytes / HTTP 000) with and without a browser User-Agent, and r.jina.ai returned HTTP 422 for it. Its content was recovered from Wayback Machine raw snapshots: the programme page captured 2026-05-05 (page's own 'Ultimo aggiornamento' 11/02/2026) and the admission requirements page captured 2026-05-11 (page's own 'Ultimo aggiornamento' 04/05/2026). These are recent captures, but they still describe the 2025/2026 admission cycle for the Italian-qualification channel.
- www.unito.it returned HTTP 403 to browser-UA curl; the central catalogue entry (code 1007M22) and the open-access master's enrolment page are reflected only through indexed search extracts.
- en.unito.it was not directly fetched; it is referenced only as the official destination the programme page itself points to for fees, scholarships and international application information.
- The compulsory minimum requirements form was downloaded directly from the Google Drive link published on the Apply@UniTo course page and read in full; it is an image-only PDF (created 19 January 2022), so its text was read visually rather than extracted.
- Per task scope, no polito.it source was used. All substantive content comes from unito.it origins.

SPECIFIC OPEN POINTS
1) 2026/2027 INTERVIEW DATES FOR THE ITALIAN CHANNEL ARE NOT KNOWN. The most recent accessible version of the department's admission page (last updated 4 May 2026, captured 11 May 2026) still showed the 2025/2026 EAS interview calendar (14 July, 17 September, 9 October, 27 November 2025, plus January 2026 on request). The structure - CLA test, preliminary application, Google Form booking at least 48 hours ahead, in-person interview, four or five dates from July to January - is very likely unchanged, but the actual 2026/2027 dates and the 2026/2027 opening date of the preliminary application must be checked on the live page. application_deadline_eu is marked uncertain for this reason. The 2026/2027 enrolment window (23 July 2026 - 14 January 2027, first instalment by 14 January 2027) comes from an indexed extract of the UNITO central enrolment page, not from a first-hand page read.
2) THE NON-EU DEADLINE IS INFERRED FROM THE UNIVERSITY-WIDE CALENDAR, not from an EAS-specific statement. The Apply@UniTo calendar shows the First admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026) as the only 2026/2027 window open to all applicants for postgraduate programmes, and calls three to five are explicitly restricted to EU/EU-equivalent/Italy-resident applicants. It was not independently confirmed that EAS specifically participated in the first call, nor was the exact Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) deadline for 2026/2027 verified on an accessible official page.
3) 'Lingua: italiano' APPEARS IN THE CAMPUSNET METADATA BLOCK of the official programme page while the same page's prose says 'Fully taught in English' and Apply@UniTo says 'Study language: English'. This is a catalogue/database artefact of the shared CampusNet template, not evidence of Italian-language teaching; the department's own admission rules further confirm that Italian is not needed for this programme. teaching_language is nonetheless flagged here because the inconsistency exists on the official page itself.
4) TWO DIFFERENT CREDIT FORMULATIONS COEXIST and applicants regularly confuse them. The programme page draws the line by WHERE THE DEGREE WAS OBTAINED (EU including Italy: a flat 18+18 credits; outside the EU: 10%+10% of the total credit load). The Apply@UniTo page, which serves everyone with a foreign qualification, merges them into 'at least 18 ECTS (or 10 percent of total degree credits/hours)'. The departmental minimum requirements form uses only the 10% rule. In practice an applicant with a non-Italian degree should be ready to satisfy whichever of the two is higher for their transcript.
5) THE ENGLISH CERTIFICATE RULE ALSO SPLITS BY CHANNEL and this is the most consequential asymmetry in this record: EU-degree holders are told explicitly that 'no language certification is required', while foreign-qualification applicants face a mandatory C1 certificate from a CLOSED list with hard minimum scores and a three-year validity limit, and are told outright that they will not be admitted without it. A Turkish or other non-EU applicant therefore faces a materially stricter language bar than an EU applicant. No exemption for native speakers or for English-medium bachelor's graduates is published; the list is presented as closed ('NO OTHER CERTIFICATIONS are accepted'), but no accessible page states what happens if an applicant is a native speaker, so this may be worth confirming with ammissioni.eas@unito.it.
6) NO PUBLISHED GPA CUT-OFF. Unlike some other UNITO master's programmes (e.g. European Legal Studies with its 98/110 and 80% criteria), EAS publishes no numerical grade threshold. Grade standing is captured only through the GPA-band question on the minimum requirements form (top 5% / top 20% / top 40% / other) and the committee's holistic judgement.
7) INTERVIEW FORMAT FOR THE INTERNATIONAL CHANNEL IS UNSPECIFIED. The 'interviews are IN-PERSON' rule is stated on the page addressed to Italian-degree holders. No accessible official page states whether Apply@UniTo applicants abroad are interviewed by video, are assessed on file only, or must travel. This should be confirmed with ammissioni.eas@unito.it.
8) LM-37 AMBIGUITY. Two distinct programmes of the same department share the LM-37 degree class - 'Lingue e letterature moderne (LM-37)' (Italian-taught, multiple monolingual/bilingual/comparative tracks) and 'English and American Studies (LM-37)' (English-taught, code 1007M22). Their minimum credit requirements, interview calendars, booking procedures and contact addresses are different. Search results and third-party aggregators frequently conflate them; only the EAS-specific rules are reported in this record.
9) NO EXPLICIT NUMERUS CLAUSUS, BUT A CAP EXISTS FOR ONE GROUP. The programme is formally open access with no overall place limit, yet a maximum of 30 non-European applicants residing abroad will be admitted. It should not be presented to non-EU applicants as unconditional open access.
10) FEE FIGURES DISAGREE ACROSS OFFICIAL PAGES: Apply@UniTo states a EUR 156 - EUR 2,800 range for a.y. 2025-26 with EUR 2,800 shown as the headline annual figure, while the programme page gives 'approx 600 to 2000+ euro per academic year'. No programme-specific 2026-27 figure was verifiable, and there is no EAS-specific fee page - the authoritative source is the central UNITO tuition-fees page.
